narrative:
The model determined that you have a 50% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability reached the threshold the bank uses to approve loans, your application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the strongest influence and pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while 59% have no checking account at all. This made your application stand out as higher risk.

The 12-month duration you requested worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward approval. Approved applicants typically ask for almost 20 months, so a shorter term is viewed more positively. Unfortunately, this positive effect was not enough to overcome the concerns raised by your account status.

Your request for a new car was the third most important factor and slightly increased the chance the model saw you as a bad risk. Only 16.5% of approved applicants use loans for new cars, whereas far more borrow for household items or entertainment.

To improve your chances next time, bring your checking account balance above zero and consider a slightly longer repayment period if your budget allows. These two changes alone would likely move your profile into safer territory with the model.
